newsitem.title: THAILAND: Student exiles deny link to Burma bomb attack.
newsitem.headline: Student exiles deny link to Burma bomb attack.

text.p: The exiled All-Burma Students Democratic Front (ABSDF) on Friday denied Burmese government claims it was behind Wednesday's bomb explosions at a Buddhist site near Rangoon that killed five people and wounded 17.
"The ABSDF wishes to make it known that despite SLORC's claim, we played no role whatsoever in this despicable act," the Bangkok-based ABSDF said in a statement.
The State Law and Order Restoration Council, or SLORC, is the formal name of Burma's ruling military government.
"The SLORC has a history of bombing its own embassies in Bangkok and Tokyo and a number of others sites in Rangoon for the purpose of discrediting opposition groups," ABSDF added.
"Given this history and its bloody crackdown on Buddhist monks in 1990, the ABSDF believes only the junta itself would be capable of sinking so low as to bomb a Buddhist temple," it said.
The ABSDF said the bombing was a plot by the SLORC to implicate democratic opposition groups and justifiy another crackdown on them.

Burma's military government had blamed the ABSDF and the rebel Karen National Union (KNU) for the blasts at the Maha Pasana Cave, where thousands of pilgrims had congregated to pay homage to a famous Buddhist relic brought from China.
Two timebombs exploded at different places at the site, where the Sacred Tooth Relic was on display, but the second one caused the deaths and injuries.
The SLORC had said its intelligence reports showed the ABSDF and the KNU had planned to destabilise the country, destroy the Relic and create a diplomatic row between Burma and China.
It claimed explosives training courses had been given by foreign elements to the ABSDF and the KNU.
The ABSF said that as an organisation that was struggling to achieve peace, human rights and democracy, it deplored the loss of civilian lives in the blasts.
"While we still maintain forces for defence purposes along the Thai-Burma border, the ABSDF considers the use of terrorism to be inimical to our aims," he added.
The group said it was seeking to develop a relationship with China and therefore would not have done anything detrimental to that aim.
